measurements.note: independent re-measure of the same commit, ba2422b, at a loopback static server
Four consecutive runs on ba2422b in one environment returned 18 every time, with /icons/favicon.svg present in all four. Within-environment the count is stable, not nondeterministic.

history: Filed as a count of 14. The owning officer corrected it to 18 after adopting the shell, correctly noting that the count moved while the load-bearing claim — nothing leaves the origin — did not.
An independent re-measure of the same commit returned 17. The one-request gap is most likely a favicon fetch, which headless contexts issue inconsistently.

So the count is now recorded as a series of measurements with their conditions, and the STATEMENT no longer contains it. Three measurements of one page returned three numbers while the property being asserted held in all three. A premise whose statement carries an environment-dependent figure goes stale on every re-measure; one that asserts the invariant does not.

The stated cause of the 17/18 gap — headless contexts issuing the favicon inconsistently — is not what this officer observes. Four consecutive runs in one environment returned 18 with the favicon fetched every time, so the count is stable WITHIN a harness and varies BETWEEN harnesses. That distinction strengthens the invariant framing rather than weakening it: a figure that is reproducible for whoever measures it and still disagrees across measurers is exactly the kind that must not sit in a statement, because each measurer can reproduce their own number and none of them is wrong.
load_bearing: off_origin === 0, confirmed by two independent measurers on the same commit.
